newsitem.title: UK: UK offers to host conference on Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: UK offers to host conference on Nazi gold.

text.p: Britain on Tuesday offered to host an international conference aimed at solving unresolved problems left by millions of dollars of gold seized by the Nazis during World War Two.
Britain's new Labour Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said there was a strong case for looking at compensation for individual victims of Nazi persecution or their direct descendants.

Cook, installed last week after the Labour Party swept back to power for the first time in 18 years, said the Foreign Office would consult organisations in Britain and abroad about how to convene an international conference.
His announcement in a statement coincided with publication of a Foreign Office report about gold stolen from individuals as well as from governments during World War Two.

Cook said that the Tripartite Gold Commission, set up in 1946 and run by Britain, the United States and France to restore looted gold to its rightful owners, would be able to complete its work as soon as possible.

The Tripartite Commission has always maintained that all of the gold it is holding was looted from the central banks of countries occupied by the Nazis. But Jewish groups have maintained that between five and 10 percent of the gold belonged to private individuals.

"It is clear that some gold taken from individual victims of Nazi persecution may have found its way into the pool. This strengthens the case for looking imaginatively for ways of compensating victims or their direct descendants," Cook said.
British officials said they expected the conference to take place before the end of the year.
They said the United States had indicated it was in favour of such a gathering and Switzerland had indicated in the past that it would in principle be prepared to attend.
"The Tripartite Gold Commission is now looking at ways of distributing the gold which it has left, possibly to indivduals," an official told Reuters.

"I imagine that the thing is to somehow get money to the victims," he added. A U.S. government report, due to be released this week, is expected to conclude that there is evidence that the Nazis sold to Switzerland gold stolen from individual Holocaust victims.
Sources close to the U.S. State Department said the report would also show that Switzerland failed to return billions of dollars worth of looted Nazi gold after the war.
The Tripartite Gold Commission has distributed about four billion dollars worth of gold to central banks. None has gone to individuals. It still has about 68 million dollars left in its coffers.
Several countries have claims on the remaining gold and would have to be part of any decision.
